learning_outcomes.text: The objective of the course is to provide insight into the technical behavior of plastics.
The study of the relationship between structure and final use properties is central.
This knowledge should allow predicting and/or explaining differences in properties based on structure.
To make an optimal material choice on a structural basis.
To translate material requirements for plastics into structural terms.

syllabus_topics: Purpose and content of the course
Basic elements (atomic forces, structure types, molar mass, determination of molar mass and distribution)
Morphology of polymers (amorphous and semi-crystalline polymers, crystal structure of polymers, kinetics of the crystallization process, measurement of the degree of crystallization and kinetics)
Technical processes and their consequences for the structure of polymers
Structure and temperature (polymer molecules in the liquid phase, temperature effects in the solid phase, transitions, characterization of transition temperatures)
Deformation and fracture behavior of single polymers
Mechanical properties of composite plastics (plasticized plastics, polymer-polymer systems, filled plastics, polymer composites)
Electrical properties (effect of electrical fields, conductivity, dielectric properties)
Thermal properties (conductivity and specific heat, thermal expansion)
Structure-property relationships of specific plastic classes
Characterization of flow parameters of polymers (viscosity, elasticity, MFI)
Overview of techniques for processing thermoplastics (general processes, continuous processes, discontinuous processes)
Overview of techniques for processing thermosets
Miscible, immiscible and partially miscible polymer blends

assessment_methods.method: Exam during the examination period (oral and written)

assessment_rules: This is a closed-book exam. Of the three questions, one will be discussed orally after written preparation.
